classification.reason: package.json with dependencies; src/ has 3+ source files; README has run instruction: 'npm ci'; Dockerfile present

executive_summary: Repository scores 86.0/100 — _strong_foundation_ band. Strongest: #01 Architectural coherence (5/5, weight 15%). Weakest: #05 Test strategy (3/5, weight 10%). Highest-leverage improvement: Add the existing test suite to the CI workflow and add at least a few component/integration tests for the store persistence and form flows..

rationale: Overall score 86.0 maps to stage=mature_platform per aggregation rules.

evidence.claim: Pure domain logic is isolated from reactivity/persistence: operations.ts holds immutable, side-effect-free functions over a plain AppData and never touches localStorage or $state.
The reactive shell wraps the pure operations and is the only layer that touches $state and localStorage, delegating every mutation to ops.* — a clean ports/adapters split.
Domain types are centralized in one source-of-truth module imported across store, validation, seed, and components; no parallel type definitions.
Layering is enforced by direction: operations/seed/validation depend only on $lib/types; the store depends on operations+seed; routes depend on the store — no upward or cross-layer reach observed.
Architectural decisions are recorded as ADRs that the code references directly, so a reader can map the storage contract and integrity rule in one pass.

strengths.point: Pure/reactive split makes the business rules testable in node without jsdom and keeps framework code out of the domain layer.
Two accepted ADRs document the load-bearing contracts (persistence envelope, referential-integrity rule) and are cross-linked from the index and the code.

risks.point: Data access is direct array scans inside operations rather than a repository abstraction; acceptable at MVP scale but a single point that would need rework if a backend is added.

up_one.condition: Already at ceiling: boundaries + enforced dep direction + ADRs + clear ownership all present.

down_one.condition: Introduce a localStorage/$state access inside operations.ts, collapsing the pure/reactive boundary.

no-cross-layer-imports.claim: The pure domain layer (operations/seed/validation) imports only from $lib/types; the reactive store imports operations+seed; routes import the store — dependency direction points inward with no cross-layer reach.

evidence.claim: Type-check (svelte-check over 4864 files) passes with 0 errors and 0 warnings.
Lint (prettier --check + eslint) passes clean on the working tree.
Functions are short, single-purpose, and read in isolation: each CRUD op is an immutable transform returning a new AppData with intent-carrying names (createUser, canDeleteUser, deleteReport).
Comments explain WHY (why time is injected, why reports are always deletable, why the period is matched against reportingPeriod not createdAt) rather than restating code.
Naming and form patterns are consistent across the route group and form components (Field/SelectField wrappers, derived validation, submitted-gated error display).

strengths.point: Domain operations are immutable and pure, so local reasoning is easy and every function fits on a screen.
Human-readable deletion-failure messages are assembled with correct pluralization, showing care at the edges.

risks.point: ReportForm relies on a state_referenced_locally suppression to seed form fields once from the prop; correct here but a pattern that can surprise a reader unfamiliar with the rune.

up_one.condition: Already at ceiling: clean typecheck+lint, intentional abstraction, low duplication, WHY-comments throughout.

down_one.condition: Introduce significant duplication of the CRUD transform logic into the route components instead of delegating to operations.ts.

evidence.claim: Multi-stage Dockerfile builds the SvelteKit app and runs the adapter-node server, exposing port 3000.
CI runs on push/PR to dev and main, doing npm ci + type-check + build with build-time env stubs.
Production deploy workflow gates on npm run check, builds+pushes a GHCR image, copies infra, and writes the env file from GitHub Secrets over SSH.
Env contract is documented as reference-only with secrets sourced from 1Password at runtime, not committed; dev/prod separation via DEV_/PROD_ prefixed secrets.
Reverse proxy with automatic TLS (Caddy) is defined for both dev and prod hosts in the production compose stack.

strengths.point: Full push-button deploy path: CI check gate, image build, infra copy, and SSH-driven compose up — dev and prod separated.
Secrets are kept entirely out of the repo (1Password locally, GitHub Secrets in CI), with .env.example serving only as a manifest.

risks.point: No application logging, metrics, or HTTP health/readiness endpoint — the frontend-only build has ssr=false so there is no server-side observability surface.
Production compose images still carry the placeholder YOUR_APP_NAME tag that the README requires hand-editing before first deploy.

up_one.condition: Add a health/readiness endpoint and structured logging plus startup env validation to reach push-button + observable.

down_one.condition: Break the CI check gate or remove the .env contract so the deploy path is no longer reproducible.

no-health-endpoint.claim: No HTTP health/readiness endpoint or server logging exists; the app is client-rendered (ssr=false) with no +server.ts routes.

evidence.claim: TypeScript strict mode is enabled in the primary tsconfig, with checkJs on as well.
svelte-check passes with 0 errors across the project, confirming the strict config is satisfied.
Domain types use const-tuple enums with derived union types and Omit-based input types, giving precise compile-time contracts (Role/ProjectStatus/OverallStatus, UserInput/ReportInput).

All external/untrusted input (form payloads, the persisted localStorage blob) is runtime-validated: validation.ts checks every field and load() verifies the parsed envelope shape and version before trusting it.

strengths.point: Runtime validation guards every boundary: form input via validateUser/Project/Report and the persisted blob via a shape+version check on hydrate.
Deletion guards return a discriminated-union result ({ok:true}|{ok:false,reason}) instead of throwing, making the contract explicit at the type level.

risks.point: The only explicit any usage is in the shadcn-style utility generics in utils.ts; it is suppressed via eslint-disable and confined to component-prop helpers, not domain code.
Validation is hand-rolled regex/field checks rather than a schema library (Zod); adequate here but no generated/shared contract artifact.

up_one.condition: Adopt a schema validator (e.g. Zod) shared between form validation and the localStorage hydrate path to give one declarative contract with inferred types.

evidence.claim: Vitest is configured and the full suite runs green: 33 tests across 4 files.
Tests assert behavior, not just shape: immutability of CRUD ops, referential integrity blocking both ways, and timestamp create/edit semantics.
A meaningful edge case is covered explicitly — 'reports this period' counts by reportingPeriod (subject month) not createdAt — matching the documented business rule.
The seed dataset is tested as a contract (all roles present, one project per status, both deletable and blocked cases demonstrable, referential validity).

strengths.point: Validation logic has positive and negative cases per entity, including malformed email and out-of-range reporting periods.
The pure/reactive architectural split makes the critical domain rules unit-testable in node without a DOM, and they are tested thoroughly.

risks.point: Coverage stops at the pure layer: no component, route, or e2e tests for the Svelte UI, the store's localStorage persistence, or the delete-confirmation flows.
The test suite is not wired into CI — ci.yml runs check+build and deploy-prod runs check, but neither runs npm test, so a broken test would not block a merge or deploy.

up_one.condition: Add the existing test suite to the CI workflow and add at least a few component/integration tests for the store persistence and form flows.

down_one.condition: Remove the vitest config and the domain unit tests, dropping below any meaningful coverage.

tests-cover-pure-layer-only.claim: All four test files target the pure $lib modules (operations, seed, validation, utils); no .svelte, route, or store-persistence tests exist.

scalability_extensibility.confidence_reason: Small surface area; extensibility judged from the seam patterns in the data/store/navigation modules rather than from observed growth over time.

evidence.claim: Adding a navigation destination is config-driven — a single array entry in navigation.ts, no edits to the shell components.
Each entity is added the same way (pure ops + a thin store method + a form component), so a new entity is an additive change against a stable pattern, not a god-file edit.
Scaling assumptions are explicitly documented and bounded in ADR-001 (single-key localStorage, ~5MB, single-user, no cross-tab sync) rather than left implicit.
Filtering/derivation in the reports list uses straightforward in-memory array filters with no per-row nested re-fetch (no N+1 pattern), appropriate for the bounded dataset.

strengths.point: Route group + data-driven sidebar means multiple engineers can add entities/pages in parallel with minimal merge surface.
The versioned persistence envelope gives a forward-compat hook for schema migration rather than a hard break on stale data.

risks.point: The single-key whole-blob write and in-memory array scans are deliberately MVP-scoped; they would not survive a real multi-user/backend requirement without the repository layer the plan intentionally omitted.

up_one.condition: Introduce an explicit data-access seam (interface) behind the store so a Supabase backend could be swapped in without touching the operations or routes.

down_one.condition: Add a blocking or per-row nested fetch into a hot derived path in a route component.

evidence.claim: No secrets in source: a grep for AWS/GitHub/Stripe keys, PEM blocks, and inline api-key assignments across src and .env.example returns nothing; .env.example holds placeholders only and routes secrets to 1Password/GitHub Secrets.
No unsafe execution: no eval, new Function, innerHTML, or {@html} anywhere in the application source.
All user input is validated before it enters the dataset, and the persisted blob is shape/version-checked on read with a try/catch that re-seeds on corrupt data rather than crashing.
Failure handling is explicit, not swallowed: deletion guards return a typed {ok:false, reason} that the UI surfaces, rather than throwing or silently dropping the operation.

strengths.point: Trust surface is minimal by design — frontend-only, no network calls, no server input parsing — and every boundary that does exist (form input, localStorage) is validated.
The corrupt-payload path degrades gracefully (catch -> re-seed) instead of leaving the app in a broken state.

risks.point: Persisted data is read back as Partial<AppData> and cast to AppData after an array-presence check; element-level shape is not deep-validated, so a hand-edited localStorage blob could carry malformed records.
No SAST/dependency-audit step or threat-model doc in CI; for a frontend-only internal tool the residual risk is low, but it is absent.

up_one.condition: Add a dependency-audit/SAST step to CI and deep-validate each persisted record (not just array presence) on hydrate.

down_one.condition: Introduce {@html} or innerHTML rendering of user-supplied report text without sanitization.

secrets-in-env-only.claim: No hardcoded credentials in tracked source; secrets are referenced via env/1Password/GitHub Secrets and .env.example contains placeholders only.

no-unsafe-exec.claim: No eval, new Function, innerHTML, or {@html} sinks exist in the application source.

evidence.claim: Lint and format are configured (eslint flat config + prettier) and enforced both in CI (via check) and pre-commit via husky + lint-staged on staged files.
The repo carries two cross-linked ADRs with a decisions index, documenting the persistence contract and the referential-integrity rule before implementation.
A committed Plan Artifact records the implementation plan, the Reuse & Prior Art check, and the pre-implementation plan-auditor verdict (Proceed after minor edits).
Commit history is conventional and intent-bearing, with issue references (feat/docs/chore, '#9'), reflecting a tracked lifecycle rather than dump commits.
Dependency hygiene is automated: dependabot groups npm + github-actions updates weekly against the dev branch.

strengths.point: The full Dynamo lifecycle is evidenced in-repo: plan + plan-audit + ADRs + conventional commits + .dynamo.json bindings, an unusually complete discipline trail for an MVP.
eslint config documents WHY each project-wide rule override exists (config-driven navigation, vendored ui/ ignore), so the lint posture is intentional and explained.

risks.point: README has drifted from the working tree: its Project Structure and Auth Architecture sections describe hooks.server.ts, login/, auth/callback/, and a /styleguide route that no longer exist after the auth shell was removed.
No CHANGELOG.md or KNOWN-ISSUES.md present, though acceptable for a pre-release template with no tagged versions.

up_one.condition: Already at ceiling: ADRs + plan + lint-in-CI + automated dep updates + usable commit history all present.

down_one.condition: Stop enforcing format/lint in the pre-commit chain or remove the ADRs/plan trail.

conventional-commit-style.claim: Recent commits follow the Dynamo conventional-commit taxonomy (feat/docs/chore) with issue references and meaningful subjects; no wip/misc dump commits.

no-changelog.claim: No CHANGELOG.md or KNOWN-ISSUES.md exists at the repo root in this snapshot.

evidence.claim: Zero TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX markers in the application source (excluding vendored ui/).
Known fragility is declared up front rather than hidden: ADR-001 spells out the brittle assumptions (single-key blob rewrite, no cross-tab sync, ~5MB synchronous limit) as accepted consequences.
No competing patterns: a single CRUD/persistence pattern is used uniformly across the three entities, so there is no architectural drift to reconcile.

strengths.point: Debt is tracked as ADR consequences with explicit rationale, so the next engineer inherits the tradeoffs rather than discovering them.
Clean, conventional commit history with no scaffolding cruft left behind (the unused Supabase auth shell was explicitly torn out, not left dormant).

risks.point: The chief residual risk is README/code drift (auth + styleguide sections describe removed code), which can mislead a future contributor about what the app actually is.
database.types.ts and the gen:types script remain from the backend-capable template though the app is frontend-only; harmless stubs now but latent confusion if the backend is never wired.

up_one.condition: Reconcile the README with the frontend-only end state and record the localStorage-scale limits in a KNOWN-ISSUES.md so the declared debt has a home.

down_one.condition: Introduce untracked TODO/FIXME markers in the domain hot paths.

zero-todo-density.claim: A grep for TODO/FIXME/HACK/XXX across application source (excluding vendored ui/) returns zero matches.
